title: Disagreement Between Parents and a Daughter's Desire to Work: Between Two Juristic Opinions
summary: Your daughter's desire to work is not a sin in itself, and the scholars have a valid difference of opinion regarding the fundamental question of a woman working outside the home—there is no single decisive fatwa. Some scholars permit a woman's work with conditions, among them: Islamic hijab, work among women without prohibited ikhtilat (mixing between unrelated men and women), and, if she is a mother, that her children's right to care is met. Discuss this with her calmly instead of outright refusal, and consult a trusted scholar to detail the ruling. Others are more cautious: they hold that the default is for a woman to look after her home, and they warn against a mother going out to work and leaving her children, and do not permit it if her children need her and no one else can care for them; even so, they permit a woman to go out when there is a need, especially when she goes out to meet the needs of others, such as teaching Muslim women, with conditions: the work is in a women's field without mixing with men, with Islamic hijab, and without tabarruj (display of adornment) or perfume. Present this opinion alongside the other, and let a trusted scholar detail her specific case.
try_this: Today: Sit with your daughter for a discussion, not a decision. Listen to why she specifically wants to work (ambition, financial need, a wish for independence), and agree to put the question together to a trusted scholar who can detail the ruling according to her actual circumstances.
reflection_prompts: Which shar'i (legal) guidelines does your view on your daughter's work rest on, and which part of it comes from social custom?
Have you truly listened to your daughter's real motivation before making your decision?
